name: strings
description: String utilities in the spirit of Apache Commons StringUtils: case, padding, graphemes, distances, wrapping, slugs, escaping

api.name: SlugOptions
api.sig: pub type SlugOptions = {sep: Str, max_len: Int where _ >= 0, lowercase: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Options for `slugify_with`: `sep` goes between words, `max_len` caps the length in characters
(0 means no limit), and `lowercase` lowercases the result.

api.name: is_blank
api.sig: fn is_blank(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is empty or only whitespace. Whitespace is the Unicode White_Space set: ASCII
tab, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, carriage return and space, NEL, NBSP, U+1680,
U+2000 to U+200A, the line and paragraph separators, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000.

api.name: is_whitespace
api.sig: fn is_whitespace(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is non-empty and only whitespace (see `is_blank` for the set); `""` is not.

api.name: contains_whitespace
api.sig: fn contains_whitespace(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains at least one whitespace character.

api.name: is_any_blank
api.sig: fn is_any_blank(xs: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether any string in `xs` is blank; false for an empty list.

api.name: is_all_blank
api.sig: fn is_all_blank(xs: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every string in `xs` is blank; true for an empty list.

api.name: is_any_empty
api.sig: fn is_any_empty(xs: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether any string in `xs` is empty; false for an empty list.

api.name: default_if_empty
api.sig: fn default_if_empty(s: Str, d: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s`, or `d` when `s` is empty.

api.name: default_if_blank
api.sig: fn default_if_blank(s: Str, d: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s`, or `d` when `s` is blank.

api.name: first_non_blank
api.sig: fn first_non_blank(xs: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The first string in `xs` that is not blank.

api.name: first_non_empty
api.sig: fn first_non_empty(xs: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The first string in `xs` that is not empty.

api.name: trim_to_none
api.sig: fn trim_to_none(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: `s` trimmed (builtin `trim`, which strips Unicode whitespace), or `none` when nothing is left.

api.name: none_if_empty
api.sig: fn none_if_empty(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: `some(s)`, or `none` when `s` is empty.

api.name: is_numeric
api.sig: fn is_numeric(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is non-empty and every character is a Unicode decimal digit (ASCII `0-9`, Arabic-
Indic, Devanagari and the other Nd blocks of the BMP, and fullwidth digits). Signs, points
and exponents are not digits, so `"-1"` and `"1.5"` are not numeric.

api.name: is_ascii_digits
api.sig: fn is_ascii_digits(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is non-empty and only ASCII digits `0-9`.

api.name: is_alphanumeric
api.sig: fn is_alphanumeric(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is non-empty and every character is a letter (builtin `is_alpha`) or a decimal
digit (as `is_numeric`).

api.name: is_alpha_space
api.sig: fn is_alpha_space(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every character of `s` is a letter or the space `" "`; true for `""`, as in Commons.

api.name: is_alphanumeric_space
api.sig: fn is_alphanumeric_space(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every character of `s` is a letter, a decimal digit or the space `" "`; true for `""`.

api.name: is_ascii
api.sig: fn is_ascii(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every character of `s` is ASCII (below U+0080); true for `""`.

api.name: is_ascii_printable
api.sig: fn is_ascii_printable(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every character of `s` is printable ASCII, U+0020 to U+007E; true for `""`.

api.name: is_all_upper
api.sig: fn is_all_upper(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is non-empty and every character is an uppercase letter (a character that has a
lowercase mapping and is its own uppercase); digits, spaces and uncased letters make it false.

api.name: is_all_lower
api.sig: fn is_all_lower(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is non-empty and every character is a lowercase letter; the mirror of `is_all_upper`.

api.name: is_mixed_case
api.sig: fn is_mixed_case(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains both an uppercase and a lowercase letter.

api.name: graphemes
api.sig: fn graphemes(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The grapheme clusters of `s`, an approximation of Unicode extended grapheme clusters (UAX 29):
a cluster is a base character followed by combining marks (U+0300 to U+036F and the other
common mark blocks, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Bengali and Thai marks, kana voicing marks),
variation selectors, emoji modifiers, tags and ZWJ; ZWJ joins two pictographs; regional
indicators pair into flags; CR LF is one cluster; Hangul jamo join into syllables. Prepend
characters and the full Indic conjunct rules are not modelled.

api.name: grapheme_count
api.sig: fn grapheme_count(s: Str) -> Int
api.doc: The number of grapheme clusters in `s` (see `graphemes`).

api.name: reverse_graphemes
api.sig: fn reverse_graphemes(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with its grapheme clusters in reverse order, so accents stay on their letters and flags and
emoji sequences stay whole (builtin `reverse` reverses code points).

api.name: take_graphemes
api.sig: fn take_graphemes(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
api.doc: The first `n` grapheme clusters of `s`; all of `s` when it has fewer, `""` when `n <= 0`.

api.name: drop_graphemes
api.sig: fn drop_graphemes(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without its first `n` grapheme clusters; `s` when `n <= 0`.

api.name: display_width
api.sig: fn display_width(s: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
The width of `s` in terminal columns, per grapheme cluster: 0 for control characters,
zero-width characters and lone combining marks; 2 for East Asian wide and fullwidth
characters (Hangul, CJK, kana, fullwidth forms), emoji and flags; 1 for everything else. A
cluster takes the width of its base character. Ambiguous-width characters count 1.

api.name: pad_left_width
api.sig: fn pad_left_width(s: Str, width: Int, fill: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` padded on the left with `fill` to `width` display columns (see `display_width`), so CJK
and emoji line up in a terminal. `fill` repeats; a fill character too wide for the last
column is replaced by a space, and an empty or zero-width `fill` pads with spaces. `s` is
returned unchanged when it is already at least `width` columns wide.

api.name: pad_right_width
api.sig: fn pad_right_width(s: Str, width: Int, fill: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` padded on the right with `fill` to `width` display columns; see `pad_left_width`.

api.name: center
api.sig: fn center(s: Str, width: Int, fill: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` centred in `width` display columns with `fill` on both sides; an odd remainder goes on the
right, as in Commons `center`. See `pad_left_width` for how `fill` is used.

api.name: abbreviate
api.sig: fn abbreviate(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` cut to at most `width` grapheme clusters, ending in `"..."` when it was cut: `abbreviate(
"abcdefg", 6)` is `"abc..."`. When `width` is too small for the marker the result is the first
`width` clusters without one.

api.name: abbreviate_with
api.sig: fn abbreviate_with(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 0, marker: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` cut to at most `width` grapheme clusters, the last ones being `marker` when it was cut; when
`width` is not longer than `marker`, the first `width` clusters of `s` without a marker.

api.name: abbreviate_middle
api.sig: fn abbreviate_middle(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 0, marker: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` cut to at most `width` grapheme clusters by replacing its middle with `marker`, keeping one
more cluster at the front than at the back when the split is uneven: `abbreviate_middle(
"abcdef", 4, ".")` is `"ab.f"`. When `width` is not longer than `marker`, the first `width` clusters.

api.name: abbreviate_words
api.sig: fn abbreviate_words(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 0, marker: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` cut at a word boundary to at most `width` characters including `marker`, which is added when
it was cut: the cut falls at the last whitespace that fits, or inside the first word when no
whitespace does (as WordUtils `abbreviate`). Trailing whitespace before the marker is dropped.

api.name: truncate_bytes
api.sig: fn truncate_bytes(s: Str, limit: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
The longest prefix of `s` whose UTF-8 encoding fits in `limit` bytes, never splitting a
character (a grapheme cluster may be split).

api.name: repeat_sep
api.sig: fn repeat_sep(s: Str, sep: Str, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc: `s` repeated `n` times with `sep` between the copies; `""` when `n` is 0.

api.name: mask
api.sig: fn mask(s: Str, keep_start: Int where _ >= 0, keep_end: Int where _ >= 0, mask_char: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with every character but the first `keep_start` and the last `keep_end` replaced by
`mask_char`: `mask("4111111111111111", 0, 4, "*")` is `"************1111"`. When the kept parts
would cover the whole string every character is masked, so nothing is revealed by accident.

api.name: rotate_chars
api.sig: fn rotate_chars(s: Str, k: Int) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` rotated right by `k` characters (left when `k` is negative), as Commons `rotate`:
`rotate_chars("abcdefg", 2)` is `"fgabcde"`.

api.name: reverse_delimited
api.sig: fn reverse_delimited(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The parts of `s` between `sep` in reverse order: `reverse_delimited("a.b.c", ".")` is
`"c.b.a"`. An empty `sep` gives `s`.

api.name: case_words
api.sig: fn case_words(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The words of `s` for case conversion. Words are runs of letters and decimal digits; every
other character separates them. Inside a run a new word starts at a lowercase letter or digit
followed by an uppercase letter (`fooBar`, `version2Beta`) and at the last capital of an
acronym followed by a lowercase letter (`HTTPServer` is `HTTP`, `Server`). Digits stay with
the letters before them (`utf8`, `x86_64` is `x86`, `64`).

api.name: to_camel
api.sig: fn to_camel(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` in camelCase: `to_camel("Hello world_HTTP")` is `"helloWorldHttp"`. Words come from
`case_words`; acronyms are not kept in capitals.

api.name: to_pascal
api.sig: fn to_pascal(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in PascalCase: `"HttpServer"` for `"HTTP server"`.

api.name: to_snake
api.sig: fn to_snake(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in snake_case: `"http_server"` for `"HTTPServer"`.

api.name: to_screaming_snake
api.sig: fn to_screaming_snake(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, the constant style: `"HTTP_SERVER"`.

api.name: to_kebab
api.sig: fn to_kebab(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in kebab-case: `"http-server"`.

api.name: to_train
api.sig: fn to_train(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in Train-Case: `"Http-Server"`.

api.name: to_dot
api.sig: fn to_dot(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` in dot.case: `"http.server"`.

api.name: to_title
api.sig: fn to_title(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The words of `s` as a title, each capitalized and the rest lowercased, joined by spaces:
`to_title("the_quick-brownFox")` is `"The Quick Brown Fox"`. Small words are capitalized too.

api.name: to_sentence
api.sig: fn to_sentence(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The words of `s` as a sentence: lowercase, joined by spaces, the first letter capitalized:
`to_sentence("helloWorld")` is `"Hello world"`.

api.name: capitalize
api.sig: fn capitalize(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with its first character uppercased (by its full mapping, so `ß` becomes `SS`).

api.name: uncapitalize
api.sig: fn uncapitalize(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with its first character lowercased.

api.name: swap_case
api.sig: fn swap_case(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with uppercase letters lowercased and lowercase letters uppercased; other characters stay.

api.name: capitalize_words
api.sig: fn capitalize_words(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the first letter of every whitespace-separated word capitalized and the rest left as
they are, keeping the whitespace (WordUtils `capitalize`).

api.name: capitalize_fully
api.sig: fn capitalize_fully(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with every whitespace-separated word capitalized and the rest of it lowercased (WordUtils
`capitalizeFully`): `"hELLO wORLD"` is `"Hello World"`.

api.name: initials
api.sig: fn initials(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The first character of every whitespace-separated word of `s`: `initials("Ada  King lovelace")`
is `"AKl"`.

api.name: split_any
api.sig: fn split_any(s: Str, seps: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The tokens of `s` between any of the characters in `seps`, with empty tokens dropped (Commons
`split(str, chars)`): `split_any("a,b;;c", ",;")` is `["a", "b", "c"]`. An empty `seps` splits
on whitespace.

api.name: split_any_keep
api.sig: fn split_any_keep(s: Str, seps: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The parts of `s` between any of the characters in `seps`, keeping empty parts, so the result
has one more part than there are separators: `split_any_keep("a,,b", ",")` is `["a", "", "b"]`
and `""` gives `[""]`, like the builtin `split`. An empty `seps` splits on whitespace.

api.name: split_trim
api.sig: fn split_trim(s: Str, sep: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The parts of `s` split at `sep`, each trimmed, with empty parts dropped: `split_trim(" a , b,,",
",")` is `["a", "b"]`. An empty `sep` gives `[s.trim]`, or `[]` when `s` is blank.

api.name: split_n
api.sig: fn split_n(s: Str, sep: Str, n: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
`s` split at the first `n - 1` occurrences of `sep`, so there are at most `n` parts and the last
one holds the rest: `split_n("a=b=c", "=", 2)` is `["a", "b=c"]`. An empty `sep` gives `[s]`.

api.name: split_last
api.sig: fn split_last(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Opt[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
`s` split at the last occurrence of `sep` into what comes before and after it; `none` when
`sep` does not occur or is empty. The mirror of the builtin `split_once`.

api.name: split_by_char_type
api.sig: fn split_by_char_type(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
`s` split into runs of one character type: uppercase, lowercase, digits, whitespace, uncased
letters and everything else (Commons `splitByCharacterType`): `"fooBar 42"` is `["foo", "B",
"ar", " ", "42"]`.

api.name: split_by_char_type_camel
api.sig: fn split_by_char_type_camel(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
Like `split_by_char_type`, but an uppercase run followed by lowercase letters gives its last
capital to them: `"ASFRules"` is `["ASF", "Rules"]` and `"fooBar"` is `["foo", "Bar"]`.

api.name: lines
api.sig: fn lines(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
The lines of `s`, split at `
`, `
` and ``, without the line endings. A final line ending
does not start another line, so `"a
b
"` is `["a", "b"]` and `""` is `[]` (Python
`splitlines`).

api.name: join_non_empty
api.sig: fn join_non_empty(xs: List[Str], sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The strings of `xs` that are not empty, joined with `sep`.

api.name: chunks_of
api.sig: fn chunks_of(s: Str, n: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[Str]
api.doc: `s` cut into pieces of `n` characters; the last piece may be shorter, and `""` gives `[]`.

api.name: common_prefix
api.sig: fn common_prefix(xs: List[Str]) -> Str
api.doc: The longest prefix every string in `xs` starts with; `""` for an empty list.

api.name: common_suffix
api.sig: fn common_suffix(xs: List[Str]) -> Str
api.doc: The longest suffix every string in `xs` ends with; `""` for an empty list.

api.name: index_of_difference
api.sig: fn index_of_difference(a: Str, b: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The index of the first character where `a` and `b` differ (the length of the shorter one when
it is a prefix of the other); `none` when they are equal.

api.name: difference
api.sig: fn difference(a: Str, b: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The rest of `b` from the first character where it differs from `a` (Commons `difference`):
`difference("abcde", "abxyz")` is `"xyz"`; `""` when they are equal.

api.name: remove_prefix
api.sig: fn remove_prefix(s: Str, prefix: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without `prefix` at the start; `s` when it doesn't start with it.

api.name: remove_suffix
api.sig: fn remove_suffix(s: Str, suffix: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without `suffix` at the end; `s` when it doesn't end with it.

api.name: ensure_prefix
api.sig: fn ensure_prefix(s: Str, prefix: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` starting with `prefix`: unchanged when it already does, else `prefix + s`.

api.name: ensure_suffix
api.sig: fn ensure_suffix(s: Str, suffix: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` ending with `suffix`: unchanged when it already does, else `s + suffix`.

api.name: starts_with_any
api.sig: fn starts_with_any(s: Str, prefixes: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` starts with any of `prefixes`.

api.name: ends_with_any
api.sig: fn ends_with_any(s: Str, suffixes: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` ends with any of `suffixes`.

api.name: starts_with_ci
api.sig: fn starts_with_ci(s: Str, prefix: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` starts with `prefix`, ignoring case by full case folding (`fold_case`, so
`"STRASSE"` starts with `"straß"`).

api.name: ends_with_ci
api.sig: fn ends_with_ci(s: Str, suffix: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` ends with `suffix`, ignoring case by full case folding.

api.name: contains_ci
api.sig: fn contains_ci(s: Str, sub: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains `sub`, ignoring case by full case folding.

api.name: left
api.sig: fn left(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
api.doc: The first `n` characters of `s`; `""` when `n <= 0`, all of `s` when `n` is larger.

api.name: right
api.sig: fn right(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
api.doc: The last `n` characters of `s`; `""` when `n <= 0`, all of `s` when `n` is larger.

api.name: mid
api.sig: fn mid(s: Str, pos: Int, n: Int) -> Str
api.doc:
The `n` characters of `s` from `pos` (a negative `pos` counts as 0); `""` when `n <= 0` or `pos`
is past the end.

api.name: substring
api.sig: fn substring(s: Str, start: Int, end: Int) -> Str
api.doc:
The characters of `s` from `start` up to `end` (exclusive). Negative indexes count from the end
(`-1` is the last character), indexes are clamped to the string, and `""` is the result when
`start` is not before `end`: `substring("hello", -3, -1)` is `"ll"`.

api.name: substring_from
api.sig: fn substring_from(s: Str, start: Int) -> Str
api.doc: The characters of `s` from `start` to the end; a negative `start` counts from the end.

api.name: substring_before
api.sig: fn substring_before(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
What comes before the first `sep` in `s`; all of `s` when `sep` doesn't occur, `""` when `sep`
is empty (Commons `substringBefore`).

api.name: substring_after
api.sig: fn substring_after(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
What comes after the first `sep` in `s`; `""` when `sep` doesn't occur, all of `s` when `sep` is
empty.

api.name: substring_before_last
api.sig: fn substring_before_last(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc: What comes before the last `sep` in `s`; all of `s` when `sep` doesn't occur or is empty.

api.name: substring_after_last
api.sig: fn substring_after_last(s: Str, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc: What comes after the last `sep` in `s`; `""` when `sep` doesn't occur or is empty.

api.name: between
api.sig: fn between(s: Str, open: Str, close: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The text between the first `open` and the first `close` after it (Commons
`substringBetween`): `between("a[b]c", "[", "]")` is `some("b")`. `none` when either is missing
or empty.

api.name: between_all
api.sig: fn between_all(s: Str, open: Str, close: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
Every text between an `open` and the next `close`, left to right without overlaps:
`between_all("[a][b]", "[", "]")` is `["a", "b"]`; `[]` when `open` or `close` is empty.

api.name: chomp
api.sig: fn chomp(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without one line ending at the end (`\r\n`, `\n` or `\r`); `s` when it has none.

api.name: chop
api.sig: fn chop(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without its last character, or without a final `\r\n` as a whole; `""` stays `""`.

api.name: strip_chars
api.sig: fn strip_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` without the characters of `set` at both ends; an empty `set` strips whitespace (the
builtin `trim`).

api.name: strip_start_chars
api.sig: fn strip_start_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without the characters of `set` at the start; an empty `set` strips whitespace.

api.name: strip_end_chars
api.sig: fn strip_end_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without the characters of `set` at the end; an empty `set` strips whitespace.

api.name: remove_chars
api.sig: fn remove_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without any of the characters in `set` (Commons `CharSetUtils.delete`).

api.name: keep_chars
api.sig: fn keep_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc: Only the characters of `s` that are in `set` (Commons `CharSetUtils.keep`).

api.name: squeeze
api.sig: fn squeeze(s: Str, set: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with every run of one repeated character from `set` squeezed to one: `squeeze("aabbcc",
"ab")` is `"abcc"`. An empty `set` squeezes every repeated character.

api.name: count_chars
api.sig: fn count_chars(s: Str, set: Str) -> Int
api.doc: How many characters of `s` are in `set`.

api.name: digits_only
api.sig: fn digits_only(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
Only the decimal digits of `s` (see `is_numeric`): `digits_only("(555) 123-4567")` is
`"5551234567"`.

api.name: delete_whitespace
api.sig: fn delete_whitespace(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without any whitespace characters.

api.name: normalize_space
api.sig: fn normalize_space(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` trimmed, with every run of whitespace inside it replaced by one space.

api.name: remove_all
api.sig: fn remove_all(s: Str, sub: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without every occurrence of `sub`; `s` when `sub` is empty.

api.name: indexes_of
api.sig: fn indexes_of(s: Str, sub: Str) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
The start index of every non-overlapping occurrence of `sub` in `s`, left to right; `[]` when
`sub` is empty.

api.name: count_matches
api.sig: fn count_matches(s: Str, sub: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
How many non-overlapping times `sub` occurs in `s` (Commons `countMatches`); 0 when `sub` is
empty: `count_matches("aaaa", "aa")` is 2.

api.name: index_of_from
api.sig: fn index_of_from(s: Str, sub: Str, from: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The index of the first `sub` in `s` at or after `from`; a negative `from` counts as 0, and an
empty `sub` is found at `from` while `from` is within the string.

api.name: last_index_of
api.sig: fn last_index_of(s: Str, sub: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The index of the last `sub` in `s`; an empty `sub` is found at `s.len`.

api.name: ordinal_index_of
api.sig: fn ordinal_index_of(s: Str, sub: Str, n: Int where _ >= 1) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The index of the `n`th occurrence of `sub` in `s`, counting overlapping occurrences as Commons
`ordinalIndexOf` does (`ordinal_index_of("aaa", "aa", 2)` is `some(1)`); an empty `sub` is
found at 0.

api.name: index_of_any
api.sig: fn index_of_any(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The index of the first character of `s` that is in `chars`.

api.name: index_of_any_but
api.sig: fn index_of_any_but(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The index of the first character of `s` that is not in `chars`.

api.name: last_index_of_any
api.sig: fn last_index_of_any(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The index of the last character of `s` that is in `chars`.

api.name: index_of_first
api.sig: fn index_of_first(s: Str, subs: List[Str]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The earliest index at which any of the non-empty strings in `subs` occurs in `s`.

api.name: contains_any
api.sig: fn contains_any(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains any character of `chars`.

api.name: contains_none
api.sig: fn contains_none(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains none of the characters of `chars`; true for an empty `s` or `chars`.

api.name: contains_only
api.sig: fn contains_only(s: Str, chars: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every character of `s` is one of `chars`; true for an empty `s`.

api.name: contains_any_of
api.sig: fn contains_any_of(s: Str, subs: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains at least one of `subs`.

api.name: contains_all_of
api.sig: fn contains_all_of(s: Str, subs: List[Str]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` contains every one of `subs`; true for an empty list.

api.name: replace_once
api.sig: fn replace_once(s: Str, a: Str, b: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with the first `a` replaced by `b`; `s` when `a` is empty or missing.

api.name: replace_last
api.sig: fn replace_last(s: Str, a: Str, b: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with the last `a` replaced by `b`; `s` when `a` is empty or missing.

api.name: replace_n
api.sig: fn replace_n(s: Str, a: Str, b: Str, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the first `n` non-overlapping occurrences of `a` replaced by `b`, left to right; `s`
when `a` is empty or `n` is 0.

api.name: replace_each
api.sig: fn replace_each(s: Str, pairs: List[(Str, Str)]) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with every key of `pairs` replaced by its value in one pass (Commons `replaceEach`), so a
replacement is never replaced again: `replace_each("ab", [("a", "b"), ("b", "a")])` is `"ba"`.
At each position the first pair in list order whose key matches wins; empty keys are ignored.

api.name: replace_chars
api.sig: fn replace_chars(s: Str, from: Str, to: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with each character of `from` replaced by the character at the same index of `to`, and
characters of `from` beyond the end of `to` deleted (Commons `replaceChars`, like `tr`).

api.name: overlay
api.sig: fn overlay(s: Str, x: Str, start: Int, end: Int) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the characters from `start` to `end` replaced by `x` (Commons `overlay`): indexes are
clamped to the string and swapped when `start > end`, so `overlay("abcdef", "zz", 2, 4)` is
`"abzzef"` and an index past the end appends.

api.name: insert_at
api.sig: fn insert_at(s: Str, pos: Int, x: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with `x` inserted before the character at `pos`, clamped to the string (0 prepends,
`s.len` or more appends, negative counts from the end).

api.name: levenshtein
api.sig: fn levenshtein(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
The Levenshtein edit distance between `a` and `b`: the fewest single-character insertions,
deletions and substitutions that turn one into the other, over code points.

api.name: levenshtein_within
api.sig: fn levenshtein_within(a: Str, b: Str, limit: Int where _ >= 0) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The Levenshtein distance between `a` and `b` when it is at most `limit`, else `none`; it stops
as soon as every path costs more, so a small limit is fast on long strings.

api.name: damerau_levenshtein
api.sig: fn damerau_levenshtein(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
The Damerau-Levenshtein distance in its optimal string alignment form: like `levenshtein`, and
swapping two adjacent characters costs 1, but no substring is edited twice (so `"ca"` to
`"abc"` is 3).

api.name: hamming
api.sig: fn hamming(a: Str, b: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The Hamming distance, the number of positions where `a` and `b` differ; `none` unless they
have the same length in code points.

api.name: jaro
api.sig: fn jaro(a: Str, b: Str) -> F64
api.doc:
The Jaro similarity of `a` and `b`, from 0.0 (nothing in common) to 1.0 (equal); two empty
strings are 1.0 and one empty string is 0.0.

api.name: jaro_winkler
api.sig: fn jaro_winkler(a: Str, b: Str) -> F64
api.doc:
The Jaro-Winkler similarity: `jaro` raised for a common prefix of up to 4 characters with the
usual scaling factor 0.1, from 0.0 to 1.0. The boost applies at every Jaro score, as in Commons
Text and the Wikipedia definition.

api.name: lcs_length
api.sig: fn lcs_length(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
The length of the longest common subsequence of `a` and `b` (characters in order, not
necessarily adjacent): `lcs_length("ABCBDAB", "BDCABA")` is 4.

api.name: longest_common_substring
api.sig: fn longest_common_substring(a: Str, b: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The longest string that occurs in both `a` and `b`, the leftmost in `a` on a tie; `""` when
they share no character.

api.name: similarity
api.sig: fn similarity(a: Str, b: Str) -> F64
api.doc:
How similar `a` and `b` are by edit distance, `1 - levenshtein / longer length`, from 0.0 to
1.0; two empty strings are 1.0.

api.name: closest
api.sig: fn closest(s: Str, candidates: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The candidate closest to `s` by Levenshtein distance, the first one on a tie; `none` for an
empty list. For "did you mean" hints, compare the distance with a cut-off yourself.

api.name: natural_compare
api.sig: fn natural_compare(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
Compares `a` and `b` in natural order, with runs of ASCII digits compared as numbers, so
`"file2" < "file10"`: negative, 0 or positive. Leading zeros don't change a number's value;
strings that only differ in them, and everything else, fall back to code point order, so only
equal strings compare 0.

api.name: natural_sort
api.sig: fn natural_sort(xs: List[Str]) -> List[Str]
api.doc: `xs` sorted in natural order (see `natural_compare`); the sort is stable.

api.name: wrap_lines
api.sig: fn wrap_lines(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 1, break_long: Bool) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
`s` word-wrapped into lines of at most `width` display columns (see `display_width`). Each line
of the input is wrapped on its own, so existing line breaks and blank lines stay; runs of
whitespace between words become one space. With `break_long`, a word wider than `width` is
cut into pieces (a single character wider than `width`, such as a CJK character at width 1,
still gets a line of its own); without it, it stands alone on a longer line.

api.name: wrap
api.sig: fn wrap(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 1) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` wrapped to `width` columns with `\n` between lines, not breaking long words (WordUtils
`wrap`); see `wrap_lines`.

api.name: wrap_with
api.sig: fn wrap_with(s: Str, width: Int where _ >= 1, newline: Str, break_long: Bool) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` wrapped to `width` columns with `newline` between lines; `break_long` cuts words wider than
`width`. See `wrap_lines`.

api.name: unwrap
api.sig: fn unwrap(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the lines of each paragraph joined by single spaces; paragraphs are separated by blank
lines and come back separated by one blank line (`"\n\n"`). The inverse of `wrap`, up to
whitespace.

api.name: indent
api.sig: fn indent(s: Str, prefix: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with `prefix` added at the start of every line that is not blank (Python `textwrap.indent`);
line breaks are kept as they are.

api.name: dedent
api.sig: fn dedent(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the whitespace prefix common to all of its non-blank lines removed (Python
`textwrap.dedent`); blank lines become empty. Tabs and spaces are different characters here.

api.name: surround
api.sig: fn surround(s: Str, q: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` between two copies of `q`: `surround("a", "'")` is `"'a'"`.

api.name: surround_if_missing
api.sig: fn surround_if_missing(s: Str, q: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` with `q` added at the start and at the end where it is missing.

api.name: unsurround
api.sig: fn unsurround(s: Str, q: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` without one `q` at each end when it starts and ends with `q` (and is long enough to hold
both); otherwise `s`.

api.name: strip_accents
api.sig: fn strip_accents(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` without diacritics: precomposed Latin letters with accents, and letters with a stroke
(`ø`, `ł`, `đ`, `ħ`), become their base letters, from the Latin-1 Supplement, Latin
Extended-A and B and Latin Extended Additional (so Vietnamese works), and combining marks
U+0300 to U+036F are removed, which handles decomposed text. Ligatures and letters such as
`æ`, `ß` and `þ` are not accented letters and stay (see `to_ascii`); Greek, Cyrillic and other
scripts are unchanged.

api.name: to_ascii
api.sig: fn to_ascii(s: Str, replacement: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` spelled in ASCII where it can be: accents stripped (`strip_accents`), ligatures and special
letters expanded (`æ` to `ae`, `ß` to `ss`, `þ` to `th`), typographic quotes, dashes, spaces
and the ellipsis made plain, and a few symbols spelled out (`©` to `(c)`, `€` to `EUR`). Any
other non-ASCII character becomes `replacement` (`""` drops it).

api.name: slug_options
api.sig: fn slug_options() -> SlugOptions
api.doc: The default slug options: `-` between words, no length limit, lowercase.

api.name: slugify
api.sig: fn slugify(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
A URL slug of `s` with the default options: `slugify("Crème Brûlée & Co.")` is
`"creme-brulee-and-co"`. See `slugify_with`.

api.name: slugify_with
api.sig: fn slugify_with(s: Str, o: SlugOptions) -> Str
api.doc:
A URL slug of `s`: transliterated to ASCII (`to_ascii`), `&` spelled `and`, lowercased when
`o.lowercase`, and every run of characters other than ASCII letters and digits replaced by
`o.sep`, with none at the ends. With `o.max_len > 0` the slug is cut to that many characters,
at the last separator that fits when there is one, and never ends in a separator. Text with
no letters or digits gives `""`.

api.name: unique_slug
api.sig: fn unique_slug(base: Str, taken: List[Str]) -> Str
api.doc:
`base` if it is not in `taken`, else the first of `base-2`, `base-3`, ... that is not, for
unique URLs: `unique_slug("post", ["post", "post-2"])` is `"post-3"`.

api.name: escape_html
api.sig: fn escape_html(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` replaced by character references (`&`, `<`, `>`,
`"`, `'`), safe in HTML text and in quoted attribute values.

api.name: escape_xml
api.sig: fn escape_xml(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the five XML special characters escaped as `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and
`'`.

api.name: unescape_html
api.sig: fn unescape_html(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with character references decoded: the HTML 4 named references (`&`, `é`,
` `, `€` and the rest of the 252) plus `'`, and decimal and hexadecimal ones
(`é`, `é`). References must end in `;`; unknown names, invalid code points and
surrogates are left as they are. HTML5's references without `;` are not decoded.

api.name: unescape_xml
api.sig: fn unescape_xml(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with the five XML entities and numeric character references decoded; anything else is
left as it is.

api.name: escape_json
api.sig: fn escape_json(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` escaped for the inside of a JSON string: `"` and `\` get a backslash, `\b \f \n \r \t` use
their short forms, other control characters and U+2028 and U+2029 (which break JavaScript)
become `\u00XX` forms; everything else stays as UTF-8. No quotes are added.

api.name: quote_json
api.sig: fn quote_json(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` as a JSON string literal: `escape_json(s)` between double quotes.

api.name: unescape_json
api.sig: fn unescape_json(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The text of a JSON string's inside with its escapes decoded (`\"`, `\\`, `\/`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`,
`\r`, `\t` and `\uHHHH` (four hex digits), with surrogate pairs combined); `none` for an unknown escape, a
truncated one or an unpaired surrogate. Unescaped quotes and control characters are accepted.

api.name: quote_shell
api.sig: fn quote_shell(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` quoted for a POSIX shell (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`) as one word: unchanged when it is non-empty
and only has characters no shell treats specially (ASCII letters, digits and `_ - . / : = @ %
+ ,`), else in single quotes with each `'` written `'"'"'` (Python `shlex.quote`).

api.name: quote_regex
api.sig: fn quote_regex(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` with every regex metacharacter (`\ . ^ $ | ? * + ( ) [ ] { }`) escaped by a backslash, so
`regex(quote_regex(s))` matches `s` literally with SSPUR's regex syntax.

api.name: quote_csv
api.sig: fn quote_csv(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` as one CSV field (RFC 4180): in double quotes, with each `"` doubled, when it contains a
comma, a double quote, a carriage return or a line feed; otherwise unchanged.

api.name: percent_encode
api.sig: fn percent_encode(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` percent-encoded for a URL component (RFC 3986): every UTF-8 byte except the unreserved
characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~` becomes `%XX` with uppercase hex, so spaces are `%20`.

api.name: percent_decode
api.sig: fn percent_decode(s: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
`s` with `%XX` escapes decoded; `none` when a `%` is not followed by two hex digits or the bytes
are not valid UTF-8. `+` stays `+`: replace it with a space first for form data.
